source.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
source.paraphrase: Mouret and Clune describe MAP-Elites as organizing search around user-chosen variation descriptors and retaining strong candidates by cell, making performance across the descriptor map visible. This motivates testing coverage, not assuming superiority.

research.mechanism_explanation: MAP-Elites uses a map keyed by user-selected variation dimensions and preserves candidates per cell rather than collapsing search onto one global best. The callback uses a limited construction analogue: each eligible rotation|feature stream is treated as a cell, proposals are interleaved round-robin, and the starting cell rotates with the paired seed. It does not score candidates or maintain elites because this fixture context exposes streams without fitness feedback.
research.hypothesis: At equal completed evaluator calls on paired synthetic development inputs, seeded round-robin traversal of eligible rotation|feature streams will reach at least as many unique valid cells as the synthetic uniform pair selector by allocating proposals across cells before revisiting a stream. This is a construction-coverage hypothesis only; the paper does not predict this callback's superiority.
research.falsifier: The coverage hypothesis is falsified if any complete matched development pair has a negative unique_valid_cell_difference, or if the callback fails to reach the same completed-call target under paired inputs and seeds. Even a positive fixture result would require separate, preregistered evidence to support transfer beyond this synthetic setting.

human_review.summary: The development report contains four matched pairs, with each arm completing 4/4 calls. Challenger-minus-reference unique-cell differences were 0, +1, +1, and +2; synthetic quality-pass differences were +1, 0, +1, and -1. These are descriptive fixture-only observations, not live or out-of-sample evidence.
human_review.rationale: The callback cycles only through ctx.eligible_pairs, interleaves each stream, rotates the initial cell by the paired seed, and suppresses repeated canonical JSON-object payloads. This borrows the descriptor-cell exploration idea from MAP-Elites without implementing its fitness-based elite archive. The comparison reached equal call targets and showed nonnegative but variable cell coverage differences, while quality-pass differences were mixed. The result is therefore limited evidence about construction coverage in this fixture; it does not establish predictive usefulness, out-of-sample return correlation, live performance, or server acceptance.
